strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why categorical distributional RL improves practical learning beyond estimating expected returns. Its discussion connects relevant work on distributional learning, optimization, and exploration.

Under the stated validity conditions, the histogram decomposition and categorical–histogram loss equivalence provide an interpretable algebraic framework for separating a mean-centered target component from a residual distribution.

The experiments cover eight Atari games and multiple continuous-control tasks, include categorical and quantile critics, and report variability across multiple seeds. Reporting both beneficial and detrimental interactions with policy entropy is useful. No material research-ethics concerns are apparent.
weaknesses: The central exploration claim is not established. Decomposing a critic’s training loss does not imply that its actor optimizes a reward augmented by that loss. Equations (7)–(9) introduce such augmentation explicitly, without deriving equivalence to standard C51 or distributional actor–critic updates. Theorem 1 concerns this modified algorithm with fixed qθ, rather than establishing an intrinsic exploration mechanism in the algorithms evaluated. This gap undermines the main explanatory contribution.

The main ablation does not isolate removal of distributional regularization. Appendix K replaces the target p with μ, and Equation (43) gives μ_E = εp_E. Decreasing ε therefore removes probability from the mean bin and redistributes it elsewhere; it does not approach a mean-only target. Performance degradation can result from this target distortion, so approaching DQN-level scores does not establish the proposed mechanism.

Cross-entropy is incorrectly interpreted as a measure of estimation mismatch across states. H(μ,q) = H(μ) + KL(μ||q), so it can remain large even when q perfectly matches μ. Consequently, the proposed bonus can reward irreducible return randomness rather than states whose uncertainty is underestimated. The distinction matters directly to the claimed exploration interpretation and is not resolved experimentally.

The bridge to FQI is limited to idealized minimizers as bin width vanishes, rather than finite-bin neural learning dynamics. Moreover, for smooth densities p_E approaches zero as bins shrink, forcing the valid mixture coefficient ϵ toward one and α = ϵ/(1−ϵ) to diverge. If p_E is zero, the nontrivial decomposition is unavailable. These implications need analysis before the decomposition can support the broader practical explanation.

There are concrete mathematical errors in the supporting proofs. Equation (39) yields an error between Δ/4 and Δ/2, which is Θ(Δ), not the claimed o(Δ). Appendix G.1 also invokes Banach’s fixed-point theorem after establishing only non-expansiveness under KL; that property alone does not justify the stated convergence conclusion. These errors require correction, although correcting the rate alone would preserve qualitative convergence.

The experiments primarily measure returns, without directly measuring visitation, uncertainty estimation, or the proposed exploration mechanism. Controls separating exploration effects from representation and optimization effects are needed. Reproducibility is also incomplete: Appendix K supplies useful SAC hyperparameters but does not specify categorical support bounds or sufficient Atari training and evaluation settings, while code release is only promised. Together with the theoretical and ablation gaps, the evidence is insufficient for acceptance.
